answer: One defense is a stake-weighted identity bond: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can vote or earn, and that deposit is slashed if duplicate identities are proven. Like a marble set on a ridge, one identity per bond is visible to all — an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while honest agents pay once. To stop cheap reuse, a slashed bond's funds flow into an umber-marked public registry of burned identities, letting peers refuse any new identity that reuses its keys, proofs, or funding trail.
